question: The library had 141 old books, and 115 were discarded. The library opened in 1952. Each remaining book was rebound into 3 slim volumes and placed on the archive shelf. Then 4 volumes, 30 volumes, and 58 volumes were added to the archive shelf. How many volumes are on the archive shelf?

A warehouse had 217 items. They doubled. They multiplied by 6. There was a distractor of 30 items. They added 22. The work took 60 minutes, or 1 hour. They multiplied by 4. They doubled. How many items?

An amount started at 34 dollars. In the morning, 56 were added. By midday, it multiplied by 7. By afternoon, 361 dollars were spent. By evening, the remaining multiplied by 9. Finally, 64 dollars were recovered. When measured in 9-dollar bundles (unit conversion), how much total?

A group started with 148 participants. In the morning, 35 dropped out. The remainder multiplied by 6 for afternoon shifts. Then they multiplied by 2 more for evening teams. The evening total multiplied by 9 for capacity planning. Finally, they multiplied by 2 again for future sessions. A sister program had 300 participants but independent planning. How many participant slots are planned for future capacity?
A warehouse had 224 boxes. They multiplied by 7. They removed 474. They removed 693 more. They multiplied by 6. They added 61. About 80 boxes are damaged, which is separate. How many boxes?
A team started with 193 points. They added 30 points. They added 13 points. They removed 26 points. They doubled the total. How many points does the team have?

A store had 44 items. They added 71 items. They added 6 items. They multiplied by 5 times. They added 34 items. They added 50 items. They added 22 items. The accounting switched from minutes to hours format. How many items?

An orchard co-op started with 17 crates and lost 8 of them to rot damage. A neighbour lent it 17 crates, and the co-op bought 47 more at auction. Every crate it now owns was filled with 9 apples from the early harvest. Sorting then removed 93 apples that were badly bruised. The rest were packed equally onto 4 lorries, and the first lorry left at dawn. The orchard covers 38 hectares, and the co-op has been trading for a dozen years. How many apples were on the first lorry?

On Monday morning a call-out engineer had 97 minutes of work booked in his diary. Before lunch one customer added 8 minutes to a job and the office booked him another 31. In the afternoon a further job added 13 minutes, and in the evening a night call added 72 minutes. The company charges 9 cents for every minute the engineer works. The invoice is written in cents rather than in dollars. How many cents will the booked work come to?

A depot had 237 crates and sent 28 of them back as damaged. Every crate still in the depot holds 4 boxes. A courier added 40 loose boxes of exactly the same kind. Each box contains 7 tubes of glue. The depot records its shift lengths in minutes rather than hours. How many tubes of glue are in the depot?

The running club meets twice a week. On Monday its members logged 67 kilometres, then 47 kilometres on Tuesday, 67 on Wednesday, 24 on Thursday, and 71 on Friday. For the season challenge every kilometre logged is worth 9 challenge points. How many challenge points does the club have?

Each morning at Greenfield Farm the packing crew fills crates with 117 punnets of strawberries in each crate, and 9 crates make up one pallet. Each afternoon 8 of those pallets are loaded onto the lorry. The farm keeps this up for 6 days of the harvest week. The weighing scales read in kilograms, but the crew notes all weights in grams. The farm has been in the family for half a century. By Saturday evening the supermarket reported that 18680 of those punnets had been sold, and the rest were still on the shelves. How many punnets were still unsold on Saturday evening?

On Thursday morning a hotel had 128 clean pillowcases in the linen store, and housekeeping added 18 more straight from the dryer. Before lunch 74 were taken up to the guest rooms. During the afternoon a coach party's rooms used another 46. In the early evening the laundry returned 21 pillowcases, and later that night a delivery brought 39 new ones. How many pillowcases are in the linen store?

Two fitness trainers, Marcus and Sophia, worked together. Marcus had 114 workout minutes planned. He subtracted 108 for time constraints. Then 2 more minutes were removed. He added 49 minutes of new drills. He multiplied by 9 for a full program. Plus 41 minutes from the morning session. And 37 minutes for cool-down. Sophia had a similar program. How many minutes total is Marcus's full workout?

In the morning, a construction site has 239 bricks stacked. By midday, 59 more bricks arrive. In the afternoon, 105 bricks are used to build a wall. By evening, a supplier bonus multiplies the remaining bricks by 5, a delivery that takes 120 minutes, or two hours. Finally, 52 bricks are used for a final section. How many bricks are left on site?

Vera's nursery had 106 seedlings, more than Will's nursery had. She took cuttings so that she ended up with triple the number of seedlings. She then bought 8 more. Every seedling grew into a plant with 4 stems, and every stem bore 7 flowers. How many flowers did Vera's plants produce?

Delivery driver Han tracked the total packages left in his van throughout his route, starting with 178 packages at the depot. His coworker, driver Osei, ran a separate route with 90 packages, but only Han's van is tracked here. By midmorning, 95 packages had been delivered and removed from the tracked count. By midday, a depot run added 29 more packages. By afternoon, a route merge doubled the tracked count. By evening, a second merge multiplied the tracked count by 6. How many packages were in Han's van by evening?

A charity shop had 159 books on its shelves in January, and by March its book stock had doubled. A house clearance added 76 more books to the same shelves. Customers then bought 289 books over the spring. A school donated 41 books in April. A car boot sale took another 85 books away from the shop. How many books are on the shelves now?

A manufacturer had 195 units. They multiplied by 6 to 1,170. They multiplied by 9 to 10,530. They added 14, reaching 10,544. They added 15 more, reaching 10,559. They added 51 additional, reaching 10,610. They added 6 final units, reaching 10,616 units. How many units total?

On Monday morning Rae made 88 cents selling lemonade, and her brother Sol made twice as much as Rae at his own stand, so Sol was ahead. On Monday afternoon Sol made another 59 cents. Sol made exactly the same amount as he had on Monday on each of the 4 days from Monday to Thursday. On Thursday evening he spent 333 cents on a comic. Sol keeps his money in cents rather than dollars, remembering that one hundred cents make a dollar. How many cents does Sol have left?

A manufacturer started with 30 units. They removed 25, leaving 5. They multiplied by 9 to 45. They expanded 3 times to 135. They expanded 4 more times to 540. They removed 137, leaving 403 units. Converting to weight involved separate calculation. How many units remain?

A gardener started with 208 flowers. In the morning, they multiplied by 7 through new plantings. Then 21 more flowers were added. The total multiplied by 5. Finally, 5015 flowers were removed for a landscape project (reflecting millions of cents in budget). A public garden had 10000 flowers but separate grounds. How many flowers remain in the home garden?

A charity marathon tracked the total miles logged by its team of runners throughout race day, starting with 140 miles already banked from early morning training laps. At sunrise, a runner dropped out, and the team's tracked count was reduced by 41 miles worth of her planned segment. By mid-morning, a relay leg added 47 more miles. By midday, another leg added 30 more miles. In the afternoon, a leg added 49 more miles. By late afternoon, another leg added 49 more miles as well. By evening, a scoring correction removed 139 miles that had been double-counted. A separate charity relay in another city, unrelated to this team, logged 500 miles that day. The team also converted its pace from minutes-per-mile into an overall hours estimate for the press release, a simple unit change unrelated to the tracked mileage. How many miles did the team's tracked total show by evening?

A participant earned 96 points initially. They multiplied by 8 for performance scaling. They added 29 from bonus activities. Then removed 299 for penalties. The remaining gained 71 additional points. Finally, 54 more were added. A top scorer had 500 points but different system. How many final points?

A manufacturer tracked output morning, afternoon, and evening. Starting with 56 units, morning defects removed 34 (22 units). Shift multiplied by 7 (154 units). Double-shift multiplied by 6 (924 units). Quality bonus added 13 (937 units). Regional expansion multiplied by 5 (4685 units). Full-year capacity multiplied by 4 (18740 units). A competitor produced 300 units. What was the full-year projection?
